> 50.3.2 comes into play when (for an example) user can upload files to a CSP-trusted scope, controls the file content but can not control the mime type. So, it has it's place and reason (it is not esoteric). It would be L3, but it is probably the easiest requirement to implement, for effort/impact it is worth L2. If there is a widespread opinion it must be L3, it can be.

Fair enough. Agreed it's super easy to implement.

> 50.7.1 is step further from basic security, it is also aligned with CSP-requirement 50.3.1 where we ask hashes and nonces from L3:

SRI (50.7.1) is fairly easy to implement and goes a long way to protect the supply chain. Since it's rather easy compared to nonces, I'd still suggest L2.

When we talk about payments, I think we are talking about L3 anyway?

> Advertisers often deliver dynamic content through JavaScript loaded from ad networks. There have been cases where attackers have managed to compromise these ad scripts. SRI would had saved their bacon.

As an application owner you don't check the code for javascript snippet for each advertisement, I think this is more sandboxed iframe area.

Also, the risk here is quite different do we talk about SRI for CSS or JavaScript.
